text:
devon: quick note: while onboarding the Go SDK I hit a surprising behavior where canceling a generator stream doesn't close the underlying connection. small repro in sampleapp/generator-cancel.

maria: ugh that sounds bad. is the process stuck or just leaking fds?

devon: process stays alive and `lsof` shows TCP FDs in CLOSE_WAIT. goroutines around the stream reader remain.

kevin: do you have a minimal snippet?

devon: yes. gist of the usage:
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
iter := client.Generator(ctx, req)
for iter.Next() {
  fmt.Print(iter.Token())
}
// users expect cancel() or ctx expiry to stop everything
cancel()
```
But the SDK's streamer defers resp.Body.Close() in a goroutine that might never run if retry loop re-spawns new reqs.

jia: noise I remember — our retry wrapper wraps the http call and uses time.After for backoff without selecting on ctx.Done(). that plus defers in spawned go funcs can lead to leaked fds.

sam: two parts: 1) ergonomics: iterator-based generator should expose Close() so callers can eagerly release resources; 2) runtime fix: make retry/backoff ctx-aware and avoid deferring closes in goroutines that can outlive ctx.

devon: +1 on Close(). as a new user I found the iterator API surprising: you expect to be able to cancel and free resources. maybe implement io.Closer on the iterator or add Finalize().

maria: agree. small API break ok if it improves DX. propose: add (it *GeneratorIter) Close() error and document that callers should call it in defer right after creating the iter.

kevin: implementation note: Close should cancel internal context and close any response body. we can add it as opt-in on 1.x minor without breaking much. also audit all uses in sampleapps and quickstarts.

jia: runtime fix: update retry middleware to accept ctx and use select { case <-time.After(d): case <-ctx.Done(): } so timers dont keep goroutines alive. Also ensure any goroutine that closes response bodies runs synchronously or is guaranteed to run on cancel.

sam: add a unit test that simulates 429s + immediate cancel and asserts no extra goroutines after wait. also CI flake that showed up yesterday might be related.

ci-bot: CI flaky test observed: go-sdk::generator_integration TestCancelLeak (failure rate 18%). opening ticket INF-1321.

devon: I'll open a PR that: 1) adds GeneratorIter.Close(); 2) makes retry backoff ctx-aware; 3) updates sampleapp quickstart to defer iter.Close(); 4) adds integration test. PR will include a short README blurb on cancel semantics.

maria: can you include a tiny migration note for users of the iterator pattern? say: "If you create an iterator, call Close() in a defer to ensure network resources are released on cancel."

devon: yep. also adding a small example in docs showing pattern with context+close.

kevin: happy to review runtime changes. keep PRs small. for the Close API please add a comment about idempotency.

jia: also grep for other usages of time.Sleep/time.After in SDK and runtime. open follow-up to fix them too.

sam: nice catch, devon. this was surprising UX for new users. once PR lands let's backfill a sentence in the Troubleshooting guide.

devon: PR #2587 coming in ~2h. will request reviews from @kevin and @jia. thanks all.

maria: TL;DR: iterator needs Close(), retry/backoff must honor ctx, fix sampleapp + test + docs.
